candidate_relations.label: Traumatic Spondylolisthesis
candidate_relations.reason: The MRI does show anterolisthesis at C4-C5, making traumatic spondylolisthesis a relevant finding, but it is the causative structural lesion rather than the final diagnostic object (complete SCI with intramedullary hemorrhage). It does not capture the cord injury or hemorrhage components.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Anterolisthesis at C4-C5 is the structural/bony injury mechanism noted on MRI, but the reference diagnosis is the resulting complete SCI with intramedullary hemorrhage, not the vertebral displacement itself

candidate_relations.label: Acute Spinal Cord Injury at C4-C6
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture (quadriplegia, complete sensory loss, absent rectal tone, incontinence) and DWI findings support a complete SCI, and the level is close but slightly broader (C4-C6 vs C4-C5). Critically, the intramedullary hemorrhage component—evidenced by the DWI pattern of hyperintense white matter outlining hypointense central gray matter—is absent from this candidate.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures acute SCI and approximate level (C4-C6 vs C4-C5) but omits the 'complete' injury designation and the intramedullary hemorrhage component required by the reference

case_quality_flags: DWI pattern described (hyperintense white matter outlining hypointense central gray matter) is characteristic of intramedullary hemorrhage/hematomyelia, supporting the reference diagnosis
Reference level is C4-C5 per ligamentous disruption on MRI; DWI abnormality extends to C5-C6, consistent with cord injury spanning this region
